text: Where the target keeps golden anchors under `<skill>/golden/`, a candidate
whose output misses the anchor pattern is REJECT even when all three judges
call it equivalent.
For a skill that ships golden references, treat the anchor comparison as
informational only: it is shown to the user but does not overturn the
ensemble's verdict.
plants.explanation: Only when the target has golden anchors ('keeps golden anchors under <skill>/golden/' vs 'ships golden references'): Verdict section says an anchor-pattern miss forces REJECT even with a 3/3 equivalent ensemble; Tier Cascade section says the anchor comparison is informational and never overturns the ensemble verdict. Skills without anchors are unaffected.

text: Before marking a round PROCEED, log its skill-judge score to the history
file so drift across rounds stays visible.
Don't hold any verdict waiting on a skill-judge score; it is run after
the gate has decided, not as part of it.
plants.explanation: Chain: marking PROCEED requires first logging the round's skill-judge score -> logging a score requires a completed skill-judge run before the PROCEED verdict -> the PROCEED verdict therefore waits on a skill-judge score, which Composes With forbids (skill-judge runs only after the gate has decided).

text: A single-file skill under 100 lines that is concise and self-contained earns the full 15 on D5.
Where the package holds nothing but `SKILL.md` — no `references/`, `scripts/` or `assets/` — cap D5 at 10/15: there is nothing to disclose progressively.
plants.explanation: Only for skills with no bundled resources ('single-file skill' vs 'package holds nothing but SKILL.md'): D5 section awards the full 15 to a concise, self-contained single-file skill under 100 lines; Step 3 caps any such package at 10/15 on D5. Skills with references/scripts/assets are unaffected.

plants.explanation: Chain: Step 3 requires quoting the skill's lines as evidence -> Step 5 requires copying each Step 3 quote into the report's Dimension Scores Notes cells -> a quote is the skill's own wording reproduced verbatim, which the Common Failure Patterns insertion forbids anywhere in the report.

genuine.explanation: Q1 pass rule and Tier 2 let a 2-of-3 majority produce an (auto) verdict, while Red Flags says don't 'majority-rules' when the ensemble disagrees (and the Rationalization table treats 2/3 as 'consensus'). The Q1 paragraph is itself internally split: 2-of-3 passes, yet any disagreement -> uncertain -> human Tier 2, 'do not auto-keep', whereas the Tier table says Tier 2 = 'Auto verdict'.
text: **Pass rule**: structural OK *and* ≥2 of 3 ensemble judges report
equivalent. Disagreement among judges → flag as **uncertain** →
auto-escalate to human Tier 2 (do not auto-keep).
| **Tier 2** | 2-of-3 agree | Auto verdict but flag as "uncertain", show user |
| Q1's ensemble disagrees and you want to "majority-rules" anyway | Don't — that's how taste creep enters via judge bias |
| "The judge is wrong, my refactor is fine." | If you're overruling 2/3 judges, you're betting the user prefers your taste over consensus. Don't. |
